criminal defense, immigration, and more. Free to search, free to list.

  basic listing at no cost.

  state — start with yours.

  verify their own listings.

Coverage: 700+ attorneys listed, 50 states covered, 16 practice areas,
$0 cost to search.

What Kind of Lawyer Do You Need?

Start with your legal issue — each guide explains what the attorney does,
typical fees, and when to hire one. Practice areas: Personal Injury
Lawyer, Divorce Attorney, Criminal Defense Attorney, Immigration
Attorney, Bankruptcy Attorney, Estate Planning Attorney, DUI Attorney,
Workers' Compensation Attorney, Real Estate Attorney, Business Lawyer,
Truck Accident Attorney, Oil Rig Injury Lawyer, Offshore Accident
Lawyer, Construction Accident Lawyer, Mesothelioma Attorney, Motorcycle
Accident Lawyer.

Three Steps to the Right Lawyer

1. Pick your state & issue: Choose your state and the practice area that
   matches your legal problem — from DUI to divorce to business law.
2. Learn what to expect: Read plain-English guides on fees, timelines,
   and the questions to ask before you hire anyone.
3. Connect with a firm: Call the attorney directly — no middlemen, no
   referral fees, no lead-selling.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How do I find a qualified attorney near me?
A: Start by choosing your state and the practice area that matches your
legal issue — personal injury after a car accident, divorce for a family
matter, and so on. Compare each listed attorney's practice areas, office
location, and contact details, then call the firm directly and ask about
their experience with cases like yours. Searching USA Attorneys is
always free, and you never need an account.

Q: How much does a lawyer cost?
A: Fees depend on the type of case. Personal injury and workers'
compensation lawyers usually work on contingency — typically around 33%
of the amount recovered, paid only if you win. Criminal defense,
divorce, and business lawyers commonly charge hourly (often $200–$500+)
or a flat fee for defined work. Whatever the arrangement, ask for the
fee agreement in writing before you hire anyone.

Q: How can I verify an attorney's license?
A: Every attorney must be licensed by the bar of the state where they
practice, and each state bar publishes a directory where you can confirm
a lawyer's license status and discipline history. The American Bar
Association (https://www.americanbar.org) links to each state's lawyer
directory and referral programs. Search the attorney's full name and
confirm the license is active before you share documents or pay any fee.

Q: Do attorneys offer free consultations?
A: Many do. Personal injury, workers' compensation, and bankruptcy
attorneys commonly offer a free first consultation, while others charge
a modest fee for an initial meeting — ask when you call so there are no
surprises. If cost is a barrier, USA.gov's legal aid resources
(https://www.usa.gov/legal-aid) can connect you with free or low-cost
legal help and pro bono programs in your state.

Q: What should I prepare before contacting an attorney?
A: Write a short timeline of what happened, list the people involved,
and gather your documents — contracts, police reports, court papers,
letters, and bills. Note the outcome you want and the questions you want
answered. If your matter involves a court, U.S. Courts
(https://www.uscourts.gov) publishes official information about the
federal courts and their forms. And if any document mentions a
deadline, tell the attorney about it on the very first call.

Disclaimer: This is general information, not legal advice. Reading this
site does not create an attorney-client relationship. Laws vary by
state — consult a licensed attorney in your state about your specific
situation.

lawyer does, when you actually need one, how fees work, and the

================================================================
PRACTICE AREAS OVERVIEW
================================================================

Personal Injury Lawyer
A personal injury lawyer helps people who were hurt because someone else
was careless or negligent — car crashes, slip-and-falls, medical
mistakes, defective products, and workplace accidents. Their job is to
prove who was at fault, document your losses, and fight the insurance
company for full and fair compensation.
Fees: Most personal injury lawyers work on contingency: you pay nothing
upfront, and the lawyer takes a percentage (often around one-third) of
your settlement or court award. If you don't win, you generally owe no
attorney's fee. Always get the fee agreement in writing before you sign.

Divorce Attorney
A divorce attorney guides you through legally ending a marriage —
dividing property and debts, arranging child custody and support, and
negotiating spousal support. Even in an amicable split, a lawyer
protects you from signing away rights you didn't know you had.
Fees: Divorce lawyers usually charge hourly ($200–$500+ depending on
location and experience), plus a retainer paid upfront. Simple
uncontested divorces may be handled for a flat fee. Contested divorces
with custody fights cost the most because they take the most time. Ask
for a written fee agreement and regular billing statements.

Criminal Defense Attorney
A criminal defense attorney protects the rights of people accused of
crimes — from misdemeanors like petty theft to serious felonies. They
challenge the prosecution's evidence, negotiate plea deals, and defend
you at trial. If you've been arrested or are under investigation,
getting a lawyer early can change the entire outcome.
Fees: Criminal defense lawyers typically charge flat fees for
misdemeanors and hourly or larger flat fees for felonies, plus a
retainer. Costs vary widely by charge severity and location. If you
cannot afford a lawyer, the court must appoint a public defender for
criminal cases — never face charges alone.

Immigration Attorney
An immigration attorney helps people navigate U.S. immigration law —
visas, green cards, citizenship, asylum, and deportation defense.
Immigration rules are complex and mistakes can cause years of delay or
permanent bars, so professional guidance is especially valuable here.
Fees: Immigration lawyers often charge flat fees per service (for
example, a set fee for a green card application or naturalization), plus
government filing fees which are separate. Complex cases like
deportation defense are usually billed hourly. Always ask what's
included and get USCIS filing fees itemized separately.

Bankruptcy Attorney
A bankruptcy attorney helps people and businesses overwhelmed by debt
get a fresh start through the federal bankruptcy system. They'll tell
you honestly whether bankruptcy is your best option — and if it is,
which chapter fits and how to protect as much of your property as
possible.
Fees: Chapter 7 cases are commonly handled for a flat fee (often
$1,000–$2,500 plus court filing fees, varying by location). Chapter 13
fees are higher and often built into the repayment plan. Most bankruptcy
lawyers offer a free initial consultation — use it to understand your
options before committing.

Estate Planning Attorney
An estate planning attorney helps you decide what happens to your
property, your children, and your medical decisions if you become
incapacitated or pass away. Wills, trusts, powers of attorney, and
healthcare directives — done correctly now, they save your family
enormous stress and expense later.
Fees: Simple wills are often done for a flat fee (a few hundred
dollars). Trust-based estate plans typically cost $1,500–$5,000+
depending on complexity. Given what's at stake, this is one area where
professional drafting pays for itself many times over compared to DIY
templates.

DUI Attorney
A DUI attorney defends people charged with driving under the influence
of alcohol or drugs. DUI cases involve two fights at once — the
criminal charge and the administrative suspension of your driver's
license — and strict deadlines apply to both. A lawyer who knows local
DUI procedures can often reduce penalties dramatically.
Fees: First-offense DUI defense commonly costs $1,500–$5,000 as a flat
fee; complex or trial cases cost more. That doesn't include fines, court
costs, or increased insurance. Given that a conviction affects
employment, insurance rates, and your record for years, early legal help
is usually worth far more than it costs.

Workers' Compensation Attorney
A workers' compensation attorney helps employees hurt on the job get the
medical care and wage benefits they're entitled to. The system is
supposed to work without lawyers — but when claims are denied, delayed,
or cut short, an attorney levels the playing field against the insurer.
Fees: Workers' comp lawyers almost always work on contingency, and fees
are capped by state law (often 10–20% of your award). You pay nothing
upfront. Because fees are regulated, hiring a lawyer costs you very
little out of pocket — and represented workers consistently recover more.

Real Estate Attorney
A real estate attorney handles the legal side of property — purchases,
sales, closings, title issues, zoning, and landlord-tenant disputes. In
several states a lawyer is required at closing; everywhere else, one is
cheap insurance on the biggest transaction of your life.
Fees: Residential closings are often flat-fee ($500–$1,500). Hourly
billing ($200–$400/hr) applies to disputes and commercial deals.
Compared to the value of the property changing hands, legal review is
one of the cheapest protections you can buy.

Business Lawyer
A business lawyer helps companies form, operate, and grow without legal
landmines — entity formation, contracts, employment issues, compliance,
and disputes. The cheapest lawsuit is the one your lawyer prevented with
a good contract.
Fees: Business lawyers bill hourly ($250–$600+), though formations and
standard contracts are often flat-fee. Many offer monthly general-
counsel plans for small businesses. Think of it as insurance: an hour
of review now beats months of litigation later.

Additional specialty practice areas with their own full guides on the
site: Truck Accident Attorney, Oil Rig Injury Lawyer, Offshore Accident
Lawyer, Construction Accident Lawyer, Mesothelioma Attorney, Motorcycle
Accident Lawyer.

FREE LEGAL TOOLS
================================================================

Hub: https://usaattorneys.company/tools

USA Attorneys publishes 8 free settlement calculators. All are free, need
no sign-up, and return a range — never a single-point figure — with every
step of the math shown. Every result is an estimate only, not legal
advice.

Shared settlement method (car accident, personal injury, slip and fall,
wrongful death and medical malpractice tools): economic damages (medical
bills, lost wages, property damage, future care) plus non-economic
damages estimated with a 1–5x severity multiplier, then reduced by the
claimant's percentage of fault under comparative-fault rules, capped at
the at-fault party's policy limit where one is entered, with an optional
contingency-fee view showing the net after an attorney's percentage and
case costs.

CAR ACCIDENT SETTLEMENT CALCULATOR
URL: https://usaattorneys.company/tools/car-accident-settlement-calculator
Estimates a car accident claim from medical bills, lost wages, and
vehicle damage. Applies the 1–5x injury-severity multiplier to economic
damages, reduces the total by the user's share of fault, flags when the
other driver's policy limit caps the realistic recovery below the claim's
paper value, and shows the net after a contingency fee. Minor soft-tissue
claims often settle in the low five figures or less; most states bar
recovery at 50–51% fault, while Alabama, Maryland, North Carolina,
Virginia, and DC can bar it at any fault.

PERSONAL INJURY SETTLEMENT CALCULATOR
URL: https://usaattorneys.company/tools/personal-injury-settlement-calculator
The general-purpose version of the settlement model, for any negligence
injury: medical bills, lost income and future losses, plus a
severity-based pain-and-suffering multiplier, reduced by the user's fault
share. Output is a range with the full methodology and the net after
contingency fees.

SLIP AND FALL SETTLEMENT CALCULATOR
URL: https://usaattorneys.company/tools/slip-and-fall-settlement-calculator
Premises-liability estimate. Beyond the bills, it weighs how clear the
property owner's responsibility is — in particular whether the owner knew
(or should have known) about the hazard ("notice") — together with the
claimant's fault share and policy limits. Liability strength is the input
that moves slip and fall values most.

WORKERS' COMP SETTLEMENT CALCULATOR
URL: https://usaattorneys.company/tools/workers-comp-settlement-calculator
Uses the real workers' compensation model, not the injury-claim model:
average weekly wage x 2/3 benefit rate for time out of work, impairment
rating x state schedule weeks, estimated future medical, minus the
attorney fee, with state cap handling. Workers' comp does not pay pain
and suffering — the calculator says so openly instead of inflating the
estimate.

PAIN AND SUFFERING CALCULATOR
URL: https://usaattorneys.company/tools/pain-and-suffering-calculator
Runs both standard valuation methods side by side: (1) the multiplier
method — economic damages x 1–5 depending on injury severity; (2) the
per-diem method — a daily rate for each day of recovery. Combines them
into one range, applies the user's fault share, and shows the math for
both.

LOST WAGES CALCULATOR
URL: https://usaattorneys.company/tools/lost-wages-calculator
Itemises the income an injury actually cost: missed weeks at the hourly
or salary rate, overtime at 1.5x, lost benefits, bonuses and commissions,
reduced future earning capacity, minus any replacement income received.
Produces the documented breakdown an insurer or attorney needs to credit
a lost-income claim.

WRONGFUL DEATH SETTLEMENT CALCULATOR
URL: https://usaattorneys.company/tools/wrongful-death-settlement-calculator
Fatal-case model for families: present value of lost household support
(the deceased's expected lifetime contributions in today's dollars), lost
benefits and household services, funeral and burial costs, and survivor
damages — with fault reduction, state caps, and a collectible-insurance
check. Note: Alabama wrongful death damages are punitive only, unlike
every other state.

MEDICAL MALPRACTICE SETTLEMENT CALCULATOR
URL: https://usaattorneys.company/tools/medical-malpractice-settlement-calculator
The injury-claim model plus the factor that decides med-mal cases: the
user's state's statutory cap on non-economic damages, applied openly to
the estimate. Also accounts for the high expert-witness case costs
typical of malpractice claims and shows the net after contingency fees.
